cards.text: Paul is writing a letter to the church of God in Corinth (1 Corinthians 1:1-2). He's spent a good while on how they should run their gatherings. Now he switches gears to the BIG one: the gospel he preached to them.

cards.question: The gospel Paul brings up here is brand new to the Corinthians.

cards.text: Paul is reminding them. They received this gospel, they stand firm in it, and Paul says by this gospel they are saved.

cards.question: Paul puts an "if" on it. The Corinthians are saved by this gospel if they do what?

answers.text: Hold firmly to the word he preached
Keep every feast in the law

cards.text: Otherwise, Paul says, they have believed in vain. Then he gets to what he calls "of first importance", and friend, when Paul says FIRST importance, you put the phone DOWN.

cards.question: Before Paul lists what's of first importance, he says where this message came from. How did Paul get it?

answers.text: He received it and passed it on
He worked it out on his own
He learned it from the Corinthians

cards.question: First thing on Paul's list: Christ died for our ___, according to the Scriptures.

cards.text: Christ died, according to the Scriptures. Then He was buried, and friend, if the list stopped THERE, this would be the saddest letter ever written.

cards.question: But Paul's list keeps going: Christ was raised. When?
Paul says Christ being raised happened according to the Scriptures, just like His death.

cards.text: Now Paul brings the receipts: the people who saw Christ after He was raised. First, He appeared to Cephas, that's Peter (John 1:42).

cards.question: After the risen Christ appears to Peter, who sees Him next on Paul's list?
Then Paul names a whole crowd. How many brothers see the risen Christ at once?

cards.text: More than five hundred. AT ONCE. Friend, I can't get six people in a group chat to see the same message, and here's five hundred seeing the risen Christ at the same time!

cards.question: Paul says most of those five hundred brothers are still living when he writes this letter.

cards.text: Then Christ appears to James, and then to all the apostles. And Paul's got one more name for the list.

cards.question: Last of all, the risen Christ appears to Paul, the man writing this letter.

cards.text: Paul says it happened to him "as to one of untimely birth." Then he calls himself the least of the apostles, unworthy to even be called one, and he's got a history he hasn't forgotten.

cards.question: Why does Paul say he's unworthy to be called an apostle?

answers.text: He persecuted the church of God
He was the youngest of them

cards.text: Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer feeling like the least of anything, and the expired coupon next to me had MORE confidence than I did. But Paul doesn't stay down there.

cards.question: Paul calls himself the least of the apostles. So what does he say made him what he is now?
Paul says he worked harder than all of the other apostles.

cards.text: Then Paul adds, "yet not I, but the grace of God that was with me." Friend, a worn-out stamper doesn't sharpen his own edges, and believe me, I TRIED.

cards.question: Whether it was Paul or the other apostles, this is what they ___, and this is what the Corinthians believed.

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Keep that oven warm, friend, because Paul's not done with this teaching. Not even close.

findings.problem: "He's spent a good while on how they should run their gatherings" states a Bible fact from earlier in the letter (1 Corinthians 11-14) without a reference.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Paul appears for the first time without being introduced. The card never says who he is, such as an apostle (1 Corinthians 1:1).

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Card 1 ends with "the gospel he preached to them." That gives away the answer to card 2's true or false, which asks whether the gospel is brand new to the Corinthians.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats the answer to card 3 ("More than five hundred. AT ONCE.") and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage.
James appears for the first time without being introduced. The card never says who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "He's got a history he hasn't forgotten" states Paul's inner state as fact. The text doesn't say it.

rule.text: He can guess at a feeling, marked as his own ("I think," "I bet"). Never as fact.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about the junk drawer plus a transition. It tells no part of the passage, even though it cites 1 Corinthians 15:9.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.
